title: Find the Redundant Directed Connection
statement: You are given a directed graph that started as a rooted tree on nodes labeled 1..n: every edge points from a parent to its child, exactly one node (the root) has no parent, and every other node has exactly one parent. Someone then added a single extra directed edge, so the graph now has exactly n edges, given as a list edges where edges[i] = [u, v] means there is a directed edge from u (the parent) to v (the child). Return the one edge that can be removed so that the remaining n-1 edges again form a valid rooted tree. If more than one edge could be removed to achieve this, return the edge that appears last in the input list. The answer is always returned as a list [u, v] using the exact orientation and values from the input. A valid answer always exists.
hints: The extra edge breaks the tree in one of two ways: it either gives some node a second parent, or it creates a directed cycle (or both at once). Can you detect each condition separately before deciding what to remove?

First scan once to find any node with two incoming edges, recording both candidate edges cand1 (the earlier one) and cand2 (the later one). Then run union-find over the edges while skipping cand2, treating a union that connects two already-connected nodes as a cycle.

If skipping cand2 produces no cycle, the extra edge was purely the second-parent edge, so return cand2. If a cycle does appear and a two-parent node existed, the earlier parent edge cand1 is the culprit, so return it. If a cycle appears but no node had two parents, return the edge that closed the cycle.
